# SLAM and Tracking

Also called: Online 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM, Gaussian SLAM, RGB-D Gaussian SLAM

## Overview
SLAM and Tracking in the context of [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) enables [simultaneous localization and mapping](#9268-slam-and-mapping.md) by jointly optimizing camera poses and Gaussian parameters from a stream of incoming images [S1, unofficial][S2]. It solves the problem of reconstructing dynamic or large-scale scenes in real-time or near-real-time, where traditional batch optimization is infeasible [S1, unofficial][S2]. What sets it apart from offline 3DGS is the use of a sliding window of keyframes and incremental updates, allowing the system to maintain a consistent map while tracking camera motion without re-optimizing the entire history [S1, unofficial][S2].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism relies on maintaining a sparse set of keyframes $W_k$ that span a wide baseline to provide multiview constraints, while discarding redundant frames with low overlap [S1, unofficial][S2]. The system performs joint optimization of camera poses and Gaussian attributes within this window [S1, unofficial][S2]. Key principles include:

1.  **[Keyframe Selection](#16758-keyframe-selection.md):** Frames are selected as keyframes based on covisibility metrics or geometric displacement, ensuring sufficient parallax for robust pose estimation [S1, unofficial][S2].
2.  **Incremental Mapping:** New Gaussians are initialized from new keyframes, often via [back-projection](#2450-back-projection.md) of depth or rendering with low variance [S1, unofficial][S2].
3.  **Sliding Window Optimization:** Only the Gaussians and poses within the current keyframe window are jointly optimized, mitigating catastrophic forgetting and computational cost [S1, unofficial][S2].
4.  **Visibility-Aware Tracking:** Tracking utilizes the [Gaussian rasterization](#17476-gaussian-rasterization-forward.md) visibility (accumulated alpha $\alpha < 0.5$) to handle occlusions naturally [S1, unofficial][S2].

## Subtopics

### [Keyframe Management](10081-keyframe-management.md)
[Keyframe management](#10081-keyframe-management.md) maintains a small, computationally feasible sliding window $W_k$ of camera poses and corresponding Gaussian states to enable joint optimization in online 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM. It solves the infeasibility of jointly optimizing all captured frames by selecting non-redundant keyframes that span a wide baseline for multiview constraints while discarding those with low overlap. It differs from fixed-interval or purely heuristic insertion by explicitly measuring covisibility via Gaussian rasterization visibility or voxel allocation ratios. See [Keyframe Management](10081-keyframe-management.md) for algorithmic details.

### WildGS-SLAM
A robust monocular RGB 3DGS-SLAM for dynamic in-the-wild scenes [S1, unofficial]. Uses a shallow MLP over DINOv2 features to predict an uncertainty map that guides dynamic-object removal during tracking and mapping, feeding uncertainty-aware dense [bundle adjustment](#8540-bundle-adjustment.md) and Gaussian-map optimization [S1, unofficial]. Marked as 2026 SOTA update [S1, unofficial].

### GPS-SLAM
An RGB-D SLAM method that represents a scene with a truncated [SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md) volume and a thin layer of 3D Gaussians near the surface for high-frequency appearance residuals [S2]. At render time, raycasts the SDF for depth plus a base color [S2]. Splats only the surface-near Gaussians with SDF-guided depth culling and order-independent blending [S2]. Mixes the two images to avoid expensive NeRF-style volumetric sampling and remove the [Gaussian depth sorting](#2845-gaussian-sorting.md) step [S2].

## Background
Originating from the need to extend 3DGS from static batch reconstruction to online, real-time applications, SLAM methods leverage the differentiability of Gaussian [splatting](#23-splatting.md) for tracking [S1, unofficial][S2]. Early works like NeRF-SLAM struggled with local editing and dynamic scenes [S1, unofficial]. The introduction of keyframe-based sliding window optimization allowed for efficient joint optimization of poses and Gaussians [S1, unofficial][S2]. Recent developments include [hybrid representations](#11926-non-baked-models.md) like GPS-SLAM, which combines SDFs for geometry with Gaussians for appearance, and uncertainty-aware methods like WildGS-SLAM for dynamic environments [S1, unofficial][S2].
